entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Diarmait Ua Briain was an 11th-century Irish king who ruled Munster from 1114 to 1118, succeeding his father Brian Boru in a bid for power in the newly unified kingdom of Ireland. This marked a significant turning point in Irish history, as Ua Briain's ascension signaled the end of the Viking Age and the beginning of a new era of Irish monarchical rule.

Ua Briain's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against his neighbors, including the Vikings and the English, who were attempting to expand their territories in Ireland. He also oversaw the construction of several castles and fortifications, including the famous Blarney Castle, which would become a symbol of Irish resistance against English rule.

Despite his military successes, Ua Briain's reign was also marked by internal power struggles and external pressures. He faced opposition from his own family members and from neighboring kingdoms, which ultimately led to his downfall and death in 1118.

Ua Briain's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, however. He played a key role in shaping the course of Irish history, and his successors would go on to play a major role in the development of the Kingdom of Ireland. The Blarney Castle, which he built during his reign, remains one of Ireland's most famous landmarks to this day.

The Blarney Stone, said to have been given to Ua Briain by the Lord of the Isles, is believed to have been placed at the entrance of Blarney Castle in 1172, during the reign of Cormac mac Carthaig, Ua Briain's grandson. This tradition has been passed down through generations, with visitors to the castle still receiving a kiss from the stone in exchange for a rhyme that they are said to remember for the rest of their lives.
